ticket: DOD-1c (plans/tickets_phase8_review.md ticket 8.3), the third of the five M2-T10 definition-of-done subtickets. 'Determinism re-check of --from-graph: re-run --from-graph, confirm byte-identical staging.' Deliverable: a re-check tool/test on the real MSCA vault proving staging is byte-identical modulo compiled_at, with the evidence recorded, plus a decision on whether compiled_at stays (documented replay-invariant exclusion) or is dropped for true byte-identity.
property_under_test: DETERMINISM of the graph->docs compiler (runner/graph_compiler.py) exercised via --from-graph (runner/__main__.py): the compiler must be a pure function of (vault, run_id) so that the graph-as-authoritative-source design (open-Q #4, 'parallel + explicit promote') rests on a replayable, non-destructive staging step (§9.5). 'Byte-identical staging' is the observable form of that purity: two independent compiles of the same vault produce identical staged bytes, save the one wall-clock publication stamp.
verification: Re-verified live 2026-07-28 (first ticket criterion). Two independent compiles of the real MSCA vault (fresh vault reads into two separate staging roots, run_id held fixed) were compared byte-for-byte. Result: of 9 staged artifacts, the 3 Part B sections (excellence/impact/implementation _section.json) are STRICTLY byte-identical, and the 6 Tier-3 architecture_inputs (objectives/outcomes/impacts/workpackage_seed/milestones_seed/risks .json) differ ONLY in the single embedded field _provenance.compiled_at (equal after that field is normalised out); zero divergences beyond compiled_at. This reproduces the ticket's 2026-07-27 recon exactly and matches the compiler's documented invariant (test_graph_compiler.py::test_compile_deterministic_modulo_timestamp; ms2-ticket8-author-proposal-graph decision entry). The new tool `python -m runner.graph_determinism_check --config MSCA/graph.config.yaml` reports: files=9 byte_identical=3 compiled_at_normalized=6 findings=0, exit 0.
run_id_observation: A fresh compile's staging equals the COMMITTED docs/** modulo compiled_at for the 6 Tier-3 artifacts, but the 3 committed Part B sections additionally differ in run_id: the committed sections carry the real run's id (msca-pf-graph-01), whereas compile_part_b defaults run_id to the config project_id (msca-pf-reference). run_id is therefore a RUN-SCOPED parameter, not a vault-derived fact -- so the determinism check must hold run_id FIXED across the two compiles (both defaulted to the same value) and compare two fresh runs, NOT couple the check to the committed docs. With run_id fixed the Part B sections are byte-identical; compiled_at is then the sole field that floats under identical inputs.

decisions.D1_compiled_at_stays: compiled_at is KEPT as a documented replay-invariant exclusion; it is NOT dropped for literal byte-identity. Rationale: (a) it is genuine provenance -- the wall-clock instant the compile ran -- carrying no vault-derived content, exactly the role of the gate evaluator's evaluated_at and the checkpoint's published_at, both of which are likewise kept and excluded from determinism/staleness comparisons; (b) the convention is already uniform in this repo -- test_compile_deterministic_modulo_timestamp pops compiled_at before comparing, and ST-1 (content-based staleness) judges freshness by CONTENT fingerprint excluding such timestamps -- so keeping compiled_at is the consistent choice and dropping it would be the anomaly; (c) 'byte-identical modulo compiled_at' is a strong, precise, verifiable determinism property that the tool enforces on every run. Dropping compiled_at would trade real provenance for a marginally simpler equality that the exclusion already delivers.
decisions.D2_check_design: The re-check compiles the vault TWICE (two fresh vault reads into two separate staging roots) and compares the two staged trees modulo REPLAY_INVARIANT_EXCLUSIONS = {_provenance.compiled_at}. To prove the exclusion is SUFFICIENT (that compiled_at is the ONLY floating field), the two compiles are fed deliberately-different sentinel compiled_at values (0001-.. vs 9999-..) rather than a shared wall clock that might coincide sub-second: the check thus proves the strong claim (even when the stamp differs maximally, nothing else does). Any real nondeterminism (hash-ordered iteration, an unsorted set, wall-clock leakage into content) surfaces as a divergence BEYOND compiled_at -> a finding. The comparison is byte-exact on the fast path and, when only the excluded stamp forces the bytes apart, falls back to ORDER-PRESERVING canonical JSON (sort_keys=False) -- so a reordered key or a numeric-type drift (1 vs 1.0) is flagged, not masked by dict-equality; and it globs ALL staged files, not just *.json, so a non-JSON artifact is compared byte-for-byte, never silently skipped (both strengthenings applied in response to the two-axis /code-review, closing its Spec residual-risk and Standards completeness notes; the honest guarantee is now literally 'byte-identical modulo compiled_at').
decisions.D3_independent_by_re_running_not_by_isol: Unlike the DOD-1b claim auditor (graph_claim_verifier.py), whose honesty is NOT importing the compiler, this tool's honesty IS running the compiler twice. It therefore imports compile_tier3/compile_part_b by design (pinned by test_tool_depends_on_the_compiler). It is still read-only w.r.t. docs/: it calls the bare compile_* functions (not the *_and_report wrappers), so it writes ONLY to the two ephemeral staging roots and emits no repo report; verified (git status clean apart from the new source files after a real-vault run).
decisions.D4_fail_closed_and_vacuous_pass_guard: The check fails closed on its preconditions: a config that compiles to NO staged artifacts raises DeterminismCheckError ('nothing to re-check -- refusing to vacuously pass', §12.4), and two identical staging-root paths are rejected (the second compile would overwrite the first). Malformed config/vault/binding surface as the compiler's own GraphConfigError/VaultReadError/GraphCompileError. A missing staged file in one tree (KIND_MISSING_FILE) and a post-normalisation byte divergence (KIND_BYTE_DIVERGENCE) are findings, not passes.

consistency_with_prior_entries: Timestamp-as-provenance is consistent with ST-1 (st-1-content-based-staleness_2026-07-27: mtime/timestamps are provenance, not content; freshness judged by fingerprint) and CHK-1 (chk-1-checkpoint-provenance-quad_2026-07-24: published_at kept in the durable checkpoint). The graph-staging non-destructiveness and the run_id/promote relationship are consistent with the open-Q #4 'parallel + explicit promote' design (tools/promote_graph_staging.py is a project-id-guarded byte copy of staging -> docs/). DOD-1c does not alter DOD-1b (8.2 claim traceability) or DOD-1 8.1 (projector mirror); it is the independent determinism leg of the same M2-T10 DoD back-half.
no_constitutional_amendment_rationale: Keeping vs dropping a wall-clock publication stamp is an implementation detail of the compiler's _provenance block; the constitution mandates neither. No phase meaning, tier meaning, gate condition, or authority-hierarchy rule changes. §9.5 (reproducibility) is directly served: determinism is now a standing, executable check rather than a one-off manual observation. §12.4/§13.7 are preserved: the check fails closed and never fabricates a pass. Recorded here per §9.4 so a future reader does not mistake the compiled_at exclusion for an un-recorded constitutional change.
change_surface: runner/graph_determinism_check.py (NEW: verify_compile_determinism / compare_staging_trees / _strip_exclusions / format_report / main; REPLAY_INVARIANT_EXCLUSIONS = {_provenance.compiled_at}; KIND_MISSING_FILE / KIND_BYTE_DIVERGENCE; DeterminismCheckError). Deterministic, Claude-free, generic/noun-free (auto-covered by the agnosticism lint as a runner/graph_*.py module). CLI exit codes: 0 deterministic, 1 findings, 2 fail-closed, 3 unexpected.

tests/runner/test_graph_determinism_check.py (NEW, 28 tests: pure normaliser + red-capable comparison seam [byte-identical / compiled_at-only float / real content divergence / provenance non-timestamp divergence / key-reorder / numeric-type drift / missing file / JSON-named non-JSON divergence / non-JSON glob + divergence]; verify end-to-end on a fixture vault [both the byte-identical section path and the compiled_at-normalised Tier-3 path]; fail-closed preconditions [same-root, empty-compile, bad config]; non-destructiveness; tempdir cleanup; DEPENDS-on-compiler + agnosticism structural guards; real-vault oracle [9 files, 3 byte-identical sections, 6 compiled_at-normalised Tier-3, 0 findings]; CLI exit-code mapping).
re_open_trigger: If a future consumer requires LITERAL byte-identity of staged Tier-3 artifacts (e.g. a content-addressed store keyed on the whole file), the change is trivial and localised: drop compiled_at from graph_compiler._build_artifact_obj's _provenance block (and remove the single entry from REPLAY_INVARIANT_EXCLUSIONS). No such consumer exists today; the provenance value of compiled_at outweighs it. Absent that trigger, compiled_at stays.
effect: DOD-1c is closed: --from-graph is proven deterministic (byte-identical staging modulo the documented compiled_at stamp) on the real MSCA vault, by an executable, non-destructive, fail-closed re-check that will catch any future nondeterminism regression. Advances M2-T10 to its final subticket 8.5 (n08f checkpoint publication).
